channel.title: INSTAR Lab News
channel.description: Research briefs, methods, and evidence from INSTAR Lab’s work in AI, quantum science, computing, health, energy, space, and the sciences.

item.title: Open data is part of the research infrastructure
item.description: Why transparent datasets, reproducible methods, and clear limits matter to credible nonprofit research.

item.title: Legal Foundations for Emerging Technology Governance
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on how legal and regulatory systems govern fast-moving technologies such as AI, biotechnology, and quantum computing.

item.title: Materials Science and the Energy Transition
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on the materials science underlying energy storage and generation—and why the path from atomic-scale discovery to a durable system remains the hard part.

item.title: Formal Methods and Trust in Safety-Critical Software
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on formal verification for safety-critical and high-assurance software—and why testing alone cannot establish correctness.

item.title: Precision Agriculture and Open Agricultural Data
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on sensor networks, remote sensing, and soil microbiome research in precision agriculture—and why open agricultural datasets are foundational to credible models.

item.title: Clinical AI Safety Research
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on how AI can improve patient safety and clinical workflows—and why rigorous safety evaluation and human oversight are essential before clinical deployment.

item.title: HPC Infrastructure for AI
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research brief on GPU-accelerated computing, sovereign on-premises AI infrastructure, and the applied systems work required for accessible frontier capability.

item.title: Quantum Sensing Breakthroughs
item.description: An INSTAR Lab research perspective on advances in qubit coherence, quantum error correction, and the path toward practical quantum sensing and computation.
